extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by combining 15 existing motion capture datasets and converting them into a unified format using the MoSh++ method.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Markers can be missing due to occlusion by the body during certain poses.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing hand markers were imputed by setting the hand poses to the average pose of the MANO model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Mocap data was converted into 3D human meshes using the MoSh++ method, which fits the SMPL body model to the observed markers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual inspection was performed to correct or remove problematic data such as swapped or mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be continuously expanded with new captures contributed by the authors and the community.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.

name.evidence: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes

description.evidence: To address this, we introduce AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.

url.evidence: We make AMASS available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de

creator.evidence: Naureen Mahmood... Nima Ghorbani... Nikolaus F. Troje... Gerard Pons-Moll... Michael J. Black

isLiveDataset.evidence: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Here we combine 15 existing motion capture datasets into one large dataset: the Archive of Mocap as Surface Shapes (AMASS).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Here we combine 15 existing motion capture datasets into one large dataset... We use an OptiTrack mocap system [33] to capture subjects with 67 markers

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We unify a large corpus of archival marker-based optical human mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.

rai:dataImputationProtocol.evidence: In cases where there are no markers present on the hands of the recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We achieve this using a new method, MoSh++, that converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset... and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep leaming.
